subject: throttling redraws when up/down-ing a numericInput

messages.author: 72212435c166bbb6
messages.subject: throttling redraws when up/down-ing a numericInput
parts:
hello group,
I have my numericInput field, and when pressing multiple up or down buttons, i get as many recalculations as clicks (not immediately, but eventually). Is there a better way to throttle these refreshes? to make them coalesce into one? 
or am I getting my reactive elements wired up incorrectly?

thanks
DG

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: throttling redraws when up/down-ing a numericInput
parts:
There's no built-in way to do custom throttling at the moment. But you could fake it on the server side like this (assume the thing we want to throttle is called input$number):

values <- reactiveValues()
observe({
  invalidateLater(500)
  values$number <- isolate(input$number)
})

Then everywhere you would refer to input$number, refer to values$number instead. Reactivity shouldn't be fired if values$number is assigned the same value that it already is, so the effect of this is to only fire reactivity when something has changed and then only once every 500 millis.

messages.subject: Re: throttling redraws when up/down-ing a numericInput
parts:
I have a simple version of my responsiveness investigation.
I am posting the code here (will figure out later how to host it publicly):
library(shiny)

default.parameter <- 50

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Reactiveness test"),
    sidebarPanel(
      numericInput("parameter",
                   "A parameter",
                   min=0,
                   max=100,
                   value=default.parameter,
                   step=10)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("parameterPlot")
    )
  )
)
and the server:
library(shiny)

options(digits.secs=3)

default.parameter <- 50
min.invalidate <- 10
max.invalidate <- 5000
t1 <- .5
t2A <- .25
t2B <- .5
tmax <- 3

clip.validate <- function(x) min(max.invalidate,max(min.invalidate,x))

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  vInput <- reactiveValues()
  vInput$oldParameter <- default.parameter
  vInput$state <- 0
  
  wInput <- reactiveValues()
  wInput$parameter <- default.parameter
  
  observe({
    if ((vInput$state == 0)&&
        (vInput$oldParameter != input$parameter)) {
      vInput$state <- 1
      vInput$oldParameter <- input$parameter
      vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t1
      vInput$maxTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+tmax
      invalidateLater(clip.validate(t1*1000),session)
    } else {
    if ((vInput$state > 0)&&
        (as.numeric(Sys.time())>vInput$maxTime)) {
      vInput$state <- 0
      wInput$parameter <- input$parameter
      invalidateLater(clip.validate(t2A*1000),session)
    } else {
    if ((vInput$state == 1)&&
        (vInput$oldParameter != input$parameter)) {
      vInput$state <- 2
      vInput$oldParameter <- input$parameter
      vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t2B
      invalidateLater(clip.validate(t2B*1000),session)
    } else {
    if ((vInput$state == 1)&&
        (as.numeric(Sys.time())>vInput$wakeupTime)) {
      vInput$state <- 2
      vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t2A
      invalidateLater(clip.validate(t2A*1000),session)
    } else {
    if ((vInput$state == 2)&&
        (as.numeric(Sys.time())>vInput$wakeupTime)) {
          vInput$state <- 0
          wInput$parameter <- input$parameter
    } else {
    if ((vInput$state == 2)&&
        (vInput$oldParameter != input$parameter)) {
          vInput$oldParameter <- input$parameter
          vInput$wakeupTime <- as.numeric(Sys.time())+t2B
          invalidateLater(clip.validate(t2B*1000),session)
    }}}}}}
    if ((vInput$state > 0)&&
          (as.numeric(Sys.time())<=vInput$wakeupTime)) {
      invalidateLater(clip.validate((vInput$wakeupTime-as.numeric(Sys.time()))*1000),session)
    }
  })
  
  output$parameterPlot <- renderPlot({
    data <- rnorm(100000,mean=wInput$parameter)
    hist(data,xlim=c(0,100))
  })
})

what do you think about this behavior?

messages.subject: Re: throttling redraws when up/down-ing a numericInput
parts:
Gah, that's a fairly terrifying amount of state-mutating code--I'd be worried about its correctness.

If you're comfortable in JavaScript, the other option is to create your own custom input binding that forks what we do in shiny.js and overrides getRatePolicy.

See https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/inst/www/shared/shiny.js#L1187 for an example; keyup and input events have 250ms debounce applied, while change event causes an immediate update.
